🇲🇽🐉🔥 Mexico won't give Washington even 1%: T-MEC talks head to a fourth round as Sheinbaum's team rejects a US-content mandate

On July 23 the US and Mexico set a fourth negotiating round in Washington for early September. Washington wants 50% of every vehicle's value made in the USA — Mexico rejected it flat. Sources say Mexico won't accept "even 1%" of a country-specific content rule, because it "opens the door" to future increases. Current T-MEC rules already demand 75% North American content and 40% built by workers earning $16/hour, with no quota reserved for any single nation.

Ebrard flipped the table: before Mexico concedes anything, the US must roll back its Section 232 tariffs — 25% on autos, 50% on steel and aluminum. The joint statement invokes "free-riding from non-parties" (read: China), but Mexico's reply is sovereignty math — it substitutes Asian inputs on its own terms, not by letting Washington annex a slice of every car built on Mexican soil.

Diversification is leverage. A country that depends on one buyer inherits that buyer's rules. Mexico is choosing options instead.

🇲🇽🎨 "If a student is rejected in that exam, we'll open the door at Rosario Castellanos — for free." "What matters is that every young person who wants to study at university can study at university. So if a student is rejected in that exam, we're going to open the door for them at the Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos, so they can study for free." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, in Santo Domingo Tonalá, Oaxaca UNAM's 2026 admissions exam broke down over "atypical results" — the university announced an in-person control re-exam for tens of thousands of applicants. Sheinbaum's answer: no rejected student left without a seat. SEP secretary Mario Delgado will coordinate with UNRC and other public universities to guarantee free admission.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>PLAN MÉXICO DELIVERS: 20 NEW INDUSTRIAL PARKS ALREADY OPERATING</u>

A little over a year after its launch, Plan México has its first concrete harvest: 20 private industrial parks now in operation — one fifth of the 2030 goal — built with over 700 million dollars from 15 developers across 10 states, El Economista reports.

At full capacity they can host more than 240 companies, joining the 477 industrial parks already running in Mexico, with demand led by automotive, electronics, logistics and light manufacturing.

AMPIP's Claudia Esteves is strict about what counts: "A park is not considered in operation until it has at least one company installed and working." Twenty already clear that bar.

🇲🇽💧 <u>XOCHIMILCO: 372 MILLION PESOS TO HEAL THE LAKE THAT WATERS CDMX</u>

Mexico City is executing seven strategic water works in Xochimilco — 372 million pesos for sanitation and drainage that directly benefit more than 42,000 residents of San Gregorio Atlapulco.

22 gabion dams now capture rainwater and infiltrate 237,000 liters per hour back into the aquifer. Crews dredged 16,000 cubic meters of silt and completed a collector nearly three kilometers long to carry wastewater to treatment plants.

The chinampa zone is not a postcard. It is infrastructure — and it is finally being treated that way.

📰🇲🇽 <u>FREEDOM OF THE PRESS IS NOT A LICENSE TO LIE</u>

Mexico's media barons are crying censorship over the regulation of a right that has been in the Constitution all along: Article 6 guarantees audiences — not just broadcasters — the right to truthful information.

As Contralínea's Miguel Badillo writes, those who do journalism have no right "to lie, deceive or manipulate," and UNESCO's ethics codes say the same. A press that packages opinion as fact and accusation as news is not defending journalism when it fights this. It is defending the privilege to keep doing it.

⚖️🇲🇽 <u>THE OLD JUDICIARY FREED THE MAN WHO ORDERED MAYOR MANZO'S MURDER</u>

"El R1," the CJNG cell leader just arrested as the alleged intellectual author of the assassination of Uruapan mayor Carlos Manzo, had been in custody before — and the old judiciary let him walk.

In November 2022, a federal judge absolved him in a pre-dawn weekend ruling, the classic "sabadazo judicial," despite five criminal records for organized crime and kidnapping. AMLO's government held his release up as exhibit A for why Mexico needed judicial reform.

He went back to running extortion rackets on lime and avocado growers — and, prosecutors say, ordered and financed a mayor's murder. This is what the reform was about.

🇲🇽🌽 <u>SHEINBAUM IN OAXACA: NATIVE CORN IS THE ROOT OF MEXICO</u>

From Etla, Oaxaca, President Sheinbaum delivered the first supports of the National Native Corn Plan, "El maíz es la raíz." Mexico has 74 registered native corn races — and the government intends to keep every one of them alive instead of letting farmers depend on hybrid seed from the labs.

"We are stubborn and we want to preserve the criollo corn, the native corn. Because if it is lost, it is like losing a part of Mexico's root," she said.

On the same stop she agreed to receive Oaxaca's Section 22 teachers at the National Palace to hear their pending demands — dialogue, on Mexico's terms.

🎰🇲🇽 <u>MICHOACÁN DESTROYS 721 SLOT MACHINES THAT FED THE CARTELS</u>

Michoacán crushed 721 slot machines that, according to the state prosecutor's office, funneled more than 100 million pesos a year to organized crime. Governor Alfredo Ramírez Bedolla led the destruction himself.

These "minicasinos" were never about gaming — they are extortion hubs and money laundries planted in corner stores and street markets. The 4T is going after the cartels' cash registers, one machine at a time.
